# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 34 THE SHIP O’DREAMS COMES TO HARBOR

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

A windy, golden dawn was spreading across the gulf in waves of radiance one morning when a tired stork, traveling from the Land of Evening Stars, glided across the bar of Seven Gulls Harbor. A drowsy, starry-eyed small child was cradled beneath his wing. Exhausted, the stork gazed around himself yearningly. Although he understood his arrival point was nearby, it remained out of view. The large white light-house positioned upon the red sandstone cliff possessed positive attributes, yet a stork with a shred of sense would never deposit a fresh, velvet child in such a spot. Nestled in a blooming brook valley, an aged gray dwelling enveloped by willows appeared more suitable, though it still felt somewhat improper. Farther along, the gaudy green residence was obviously unacceptable. At that moment, the stork's spirits rose. The ideal location had met his gaze—a small white dwelling resting beside a large, rustling firwood, possessing a curl of blue smoke rising above its kitchen chimney—a dwelling that appeared perfectly designed for babies. Letting out a contented sigh, the stork gently touched down upon the ridge-pole.
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0000 }

Thirty minutes had passed when Hugh hurried through the hallway and knocked at the spare room's door. He was greeted by a sleepy reply, and shortly afterward, Thirza peered from behind the door, her pale face filled with fear.
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0001 }

“Thirza, I have been sent by Nell to inform you of a particular young gentleman's arrival at this place. Although his luggage is sparse, his intention to remain is clear.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0002 }

“Good heavens!” Thirza uttered in astonishment. “Hugh, you surely aren't saying that everything has ended. What was the reason I wasn't summoned?”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0003 }

“Nell prevented us from bothering you while it was unnecessary. No person was summoned prior to roughly two hours back. This time lacked any 'passage perilous’.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0004 }

“And—and—Hugh—is this infant going to survive?”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0005 }

“He definitely is going to. His weight is ten pounds, and—well, just hear him. There is not a thing wrong with his lungs, right? According to the nurse, his hair is going to be red. Nell feels enraged at her, whereas I am utterly delighted.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0006 }

It was a marvelous time spent inside the small home of dreams.
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0007 }

“The finest vision imaginable has been realized,” uttered Nell, white-faced and filled with joy. “Oh, Thirza, following that dreadful afternoon a year ago, I scarcely have the courage to trust it. My heart has ached continuously from that time onward—yet the pain has vanished now.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0008 }

“Replacing Joy will be the function of this infant,” declared Thirza.
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0009 }

“Oh, no, no, NO, Thirza. He can’t—nothing can ever do that. My dear, wee man-child has his own place. But little Joy has hers, and she will always keep it. Had she lived, she would be more than a year old by now. She would be walking on her tiny feet and speaking a few words. Thirza, I can see her so clearly. Oh, I realize now the truth in what Captain Saul said about God managing better than allowing my baby to seem like a stranger when I find her Beyond. During this past year, I’ve learned THAT. Day by day and week by week, I’ve followed her development—and I always will. I shall know exactly how she grows year after year—and when we meet again, I’ll recognize her—she won’t be a stranger. Oh, Thirza, LOOK at his dear, darling toes! Isn’t it strange that they are so perfect?”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0010 }

“They would be even stranger were that not so,” Thirza remarked briskly. With everything now securely concluded, Thirza had returned to her usual self.
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0011 }

“Oh, I am aware—yet it appears like they could not be entirely FINISHED, you see—and they are indeed, down to the miniscule nails. Also his hands—ONLY examine his hands, Thirza.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0012 }

“They seem to look quite a bit like hands,” admitted Thirza.
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0013 }

“Look at the way he grips my finger. It seems certain to me that he recognizes me this early. Whenever the nurse carries him off, he weeps. Oh, Thirza, is it possible—surely you don't imagine—that he will end up with red hair?”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0014 }

“I fail to observe a great deal of hair of any hue,” Thirza remarked. “If I found myself in your position, I would not concern myself with it prior to its becoming apparent.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0015 }

“Thirza, he DOES have hair—see that soft little fuzz covering his whole head. Besides, nurse claims his eyes are going to be hazel and he has a forehead that is identical to Hugh’s.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0016 }

“And he possesses the most delightful little ears, Mrs. Doctor, dear,” Tabitha remarked. “Looking at his ears was my very first action. Hair deceives and noses and eyes undergo changes, rendering it impossible to predict their outcome, but ears remain ears throughout, providing certainty at all times. Simply observe their form—and they rest directly against his precious head. His ears will never cause you embarrassment, Mrs. Doctor, dear.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0017 }

Nell experienced a swift and joyful recovery. People arrived to adore the child, following a tradition of bowing to the sovereignty of infants that began well before the Eastern Wise Men offered their reverent worship to Bethlehem's Royal Babe in the manger. Gradually adjusting to her altered circumstances, Lorna hovered beside the infant, resembling a gorgeous Madonna crowned in gold. Miss Winifred provided care as skillfully as any mother in Israel. Resting the tiny being in his large, brown hands, Captain Saul looked upon it fondly, his eyes reflecting the offspring he had never fathered.
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0018 }

“What name will you give him?” Miss Winifred inquired.
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0019 }

“Nell has chosen what he will be called,” Hugh replied.
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0020 }

“James Obed—named for the pair of most splendid gentlemen I have ever come across—present company notwithstanding,” Nell stated, casting a cheeky look toward Hugh.
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0021 }

Hugh smiled.
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0022 }

“I was never particularly familiar with Obed; he possessed such shyness that us boys were unable to become acquainted with him—nevertheless, I fully concur with your view that Captain Saul represents one of the most exceptional and splendid spirits God ever encased in dust. He experiences such joy because we bestowed his name upon our little boy. Apparently, he possesses no additional namesake.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0023 }

“Indeed, James Obed stands as a moniker that holds up durability and won't wash away,” Miss Winifred remarked. “It pleases me that you refrained from overburdening him with a lofty, imaginative title he might feel embarrassed by upon becoming a grandfather. Over at the Glen, Mrs. William Drew bestowed the name Bertie Shakespeare upon her infant. That makes quite a pairing, does it not? Furthermore, it delights me that selecting a title caused you little difficulty. Certain people experience terrible struggles. Following the arrival of the Stanley Flaggs’ initial son, competition regarding his namesake proved so intense that the unfortunate young spirit remained nameless across a two-year span. Subsequently, a brother arrived, resulting in the labels—'Big Baby’ alongside 'Little Baby.’ In the end, Big Baby became Peter while Little Baby became Isaac, honoring the pair of grandfathers, with their christenings occurring simultaneously. Thereupon, every child attempted to determine whether he could out-screech his brother. Are you familiar with the MacNabs, that Highland Scotch kin located behind the Glen? Twelve sons belong to them, with both the firstborn and the lastborn bearing the name Neil—Big Neil alongside Little Neil within one household. Naturally, my assumption is that their supply of names became exhausted.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0024 }

“I have read somewhere,” Nell said with a laugh, “that while a poem is what the first child is, the tenth is extremely prosy prose. That the twelfth was simply an old story told again might have been what Mrs. MacNab thought.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0025 }

“Well, there is a certain merit to having big families,” Miss Winifred stated while sighing. “Being an only child throughout eight years, I truly craved a brother and sister. My mother instructed me to pray for one—and I certainly did pray, believe ME. Well, on a particular day, Aunt Nellie approached me and remarked, 'Winifred, there is a little brother for you upstairs in your ma’s room. You can go up and see him.’ Filled with such excitement and delight, I simply rushed upstairs. Then old Mrs. Flagg raised the baby so that I could view him. Lord, Nell, dearie, I had never experienced such disappointment in all my life. You see, my prayers had been for A BROTHER TWO YEARS OLDER THAN MYSELF.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0026 }

“How much time passed before you moved past your letdown?” Nell inquired, while laughing.
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0027 }

“Indeed, my anger toward Providence lingered for a considerable duration, so that weeks passed without my even glancing at the infant. The reason remained my secret, as I kept it to myself. Eventually, he started becoming truly adorable, stretching his tiny hands toward me, which made me start caring for him. However, my complete acceptance of him didn't occur until a former classmate visited to view him and remarked that he appeared terribly tiny for how old he was. My temper flared intensely, and I launched straight into a confrontation with her, declaring that she failed to recognize a lovely baby upon seeing one, and that ours was the world's most wonderful infant. From that moment forward, I simply adored him. Our mother passed away prior to his third birthday, leading me to serve as both a sister and a mother to him. That unfortunate young boy was constantly frail, and his life ended when he had barely passed twenty. It feels to me as though I would have surrendered whatever existed on earth, Nell, dearie, if he had merely survived.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0028 }

Miss Winifred let out a sigh. After Hugh departed, Lorna, who had been singing softly to little James Obed by the dormer window, placed the sleeping child into his basket and departed. Once she was far enough away to no longer hear, Miss Winifred leaned in and murmured like a fellow conspirator:
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0029 }

“Nell, dearie, yesterday a letter arrived for me from Adrian Treleaven. At the present time he is in Vancouver, but he wishes to learn whether I am able to provide him with room and board for a month at a later date. YOU understand what that implies. Well, I trust we are acting properly.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0030 }

“We have no part in this—if he desired to travel to Seven Gulls, we had no way of stopping him,” Nell stated hastily. The sensation of match-making that Miss Winifred’s hushed words conveyed displeased her; and after that, she feebly yielded to it herself.
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0031 }

“Do not inform Lorna that he is arriving prior to his presence,” she remarked. “Were she to discover this, I am certain she would depart immediately. In any case, she plans to leave in the autumn—she mentioned it to me a short while ago. She aims to move to Montreal to pursue nursing and shape her future as best she can.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0032 }

“Oh, well, Nell, my dear,” Miss Winifred remarked with a wise nod, “that remains to be seen. You and I have fulfilled our duty, and now we are required to entrust whatever remains to Higher Hands.”
{: #nw-v04-c34-p0033 }
